result.topic_en: Finding exponents x for which 2^{2x}+2^x+1 is divisible by 19 via residues of powers of 2, followed by fragment 15 (J. A. Euler) on classifying powers a^p by whether a^p-1 or a^p+1 is divisible by a prime 2p+1.
result.transcription:
174 \quad L. EULERI OPERA POSTHUMA. \quad Arithmetica.

Solutio. Cum ergo formula $2^{2x}+2^x$ residuum habere debeat $-1$, sive $-1+\lambda p$, ponamus potestatem $2^x$ habere residuum $r$, atque ejus quadratum $2^{2x}$ residuum habebit $rr$, ideoque illius formae residuum erit $rr+r$. Quaeratur ergo $r$, ut fiat
$rr+r=-1+\lambda p$, sive $4rr+4r+1=(2r+1)^2=4\lambda p-3$, unde $2r+1=\sqrt{(4\lambda p-3)}$;
$\lambda$ igitur ita sumi debet, ut $4\lambda p-3$ sit quadratum. Invento autem $r$ quaeratur potestas $2^x$ residuum habens $r$, quod est problema superius.
Sit verbi gratia divisor $p=19$ et quadratum esse debet $76\lambda-3$, quod fit si $\lambda=3$, ergo $2r+1=\pm15$, consequenter vel $r=+7$, vel $r=-8$.
I. Pro $r=+7$ \quad $2^x$ resid. $+7$ \quad $-12=-2^2.3$
$2^{x-2}$ \quad $-3$ \quad $16=2^4$
$2^{x-6}$ \quad $1$ \quad hinc $x=6$
ideoque $2^{12}+2^6+1$ divisibile per 19.
II. Pro $r=-8$ \quad $2^x$ resid. $-8$ \quad $-2^3.1$
$2^{x-3}$ \quad $-1$ \quad $-20=-2^2.5$
$2^{x-5}$ \quad $-5$ \quad $-24=-2^3.3$
$2^{x-8}$ \quad $-3$ \quad $16=2^4$
$2^{x-12}$ \quad $1$ \quad $x=12$
ideoque $2^{24}+2^{12}+1$ divisibile per 19.
A. m. T. I. p. 143—149.

15.
(J. A. Euler.)
Cum sit $a^{2p}-1$ divisibile per $2p+1$, si $2p+1$ fuerit numerus primus, tum vel $a^p-1$, vel $a^p+1$ per eum dividi poterit. Duplicis ergo generis sunt potestates $a^p$, prouti vel formula $a^p-1$, vel $a^p+1$ fuerit divisibilis per $2p+1$.
Theorema. Cujus generis fuerit potestas $a^p$, ejusdem generis quoque erunt omnes istae
$a^{2a+p}$, $a^{4a+p}$, $a^{6a+p}$ et in genere $a^{2na+p}$,
ubi $a$ debet esse primus ad $2p+1$ et $n$ quoque potest esse numerus negativus.
Praeterea vero etiam ejusdem generis erunt hae potestates
$a^{2a-p-1}$, $a^{4a-p-1}$, $a^{6a-p-1}$ et in genere $a^{2na-p-1}$
hoc autem posterius tantum valet, si $a$ fuerit numerus positivus; si enim sit negativus, hae posteriores potestates ad alterum genus pertinent. Ratio hujus exceptionis manifesta est: si enim $p$ fuerit numerus par, perinde est sive capiatur $+a$, sive $-a$; sin autem $p$ sit impar, loco $a$ sumendo $-a$, ipsa potestas fit negativa. Sicque si formula $(+a)^p\pm1$ fuerit per $2p+1$ divisibilis, tum $(-a)^p\mp1$ divisibilis erit.
Exemplum. Quia $2^1+1$ per $2.1+1=3$ est divisibile, ubi $a=2$ et $p=1$, ad idem genus pertinebunt hae potestates
$2^1, 2^5, 2^9, 2^{13}, 2^{17}, 2^{21} \ldots 2^{4n+1}$
deinde etiam istae \quad $2^2, 2^6, 2^{10}, 2^{14}, 2^{18}, 2^{22} \ldots 2^{4n+2}$.
Examinemus casum $2^{21}$, an $2^{21}+1$ divisibile sit per 43, sive an $2^{21}$ per 43 divisum relinquat $-1$, quod ope methodi supra expositae ita fiet

methods.what: Reduce 2^{2x}+2^x ≡ -1 (mod p) to finding residue r of 2^x with r^2+r ≡ -1, i.e. choose λ so 4λp-3 is a square, then 2r+1 = sqrt(4λp-3)
Worked example p=19: λ=3 gives r=7 or r=-8; repeated division of residues by powers of 2 yields x=6 and x=12
For prime 2p+1, a^{2p}-1 divisible, so either a^p-1 or a^p+1 divisible; powers split into two kinds
methods.quote: Cum sit $a^{2p}-1$ divisibile per $2p+1$, si $2p+1$ fuerit numerus primus, tum vel $a^p-1$, vel $a^p+1$ per eum dividi poterit.

methods.what: Theorem: a^{2na+p} and (for positive a) a^{2na-p-1} are of the same kind as a^p

items.quote:
Cujus generis fuerit potestas $a^p$, ejusdem generis quoque erunt omnes istae
$a^{2a+p}$, $a^{4a+p}$, $a^{6a+p}$ et in genere $a^{2na+p}$,
ubi $a$ debet esse primus ad $2p+1$ et $n$ quoque potest esse numerus negativus.
items.english: Whatever kind the power a^p is, of the same kind will also be all these: a^{2a+p}, a^{4a+p}, a^{6a+p} and in general a^{2na+p}, where a must be prime to 2p+1 and n can also be a negative number.

items.quote:
Praeterea vero etiam ejusdem generis erunt hae potestates
$a^{2a-p-1}$, $a^{4a-p-1}$, $a^{6a-p-1}$ et in genere $a^{2na-p-1}$
hoc autem posterius tantum valet, si $a$ fuerit numerus positivus
items.english: Moreover these powers will also be of the same kind: a^{2a-p-1}, a^{4a-p-1}, a^{6a-p-1} and in general a^{2na-p-1}; but this latter holds only if a is a positive number.

items.quote: Examinemus casum $2^{21}$, an $2^{21}+1$ divisibile sit per 43, sive an $2^{21}$ per 43 divisum relinquat $-1$
items.english: Let us examine the case 2^21, whether 2^21+1 is divisible by 43, or whether 2^21 divided by 43 leaves -1.
